5.10.betting_forecast: 7/4 Livenka, 5/2 Aedhmar, 3/1 Victorious, 7/1 Beibhinn, 12/1 Roeillaun, 16/1 Ballinea Star.
5.10.spotlight_verdict: Cork third Aedhmar has the experience but LIVENKA is from a smart family that Ger Lyons has done well with and her siblings have had a good record first-time out. Ballydoyle's Victorious and Joseph O'Brien's Beibhinn are the others to focus on. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: Daughter of Blue Point is a sibling of many winners, including some smart juveniles; 2-1 fav when third of 6 at Cork, beaten only a neck in total on testing ground.

Made 26,000euros as a yearling; fourth foal; half-sister to 12.5f/14.3f winner Gangster Granny (RPR 80); dam Group-placed 6f 2yo winner (101), half-sister to Listed-placed French/Italian 7.5f-1m4f winner Jack Boy, out of unraced half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Rajeem; missed last month's intended debut at Curragh (coughing); that Egan doesn't ride is not a positive sign.

First foal; dam placed 7f (inc AW 2yo; RPR 81), half-sister to winners Hispanic (useful 5f 2yo/6f, by No Nay Never), Ghaziyah (1m) and Mamluk (French 1m4f), out of 8.5f winning half-sister to French 2,000 Guineas winner Aussie Rules; yard red-hot and first 2yo runner hit the target lately.

Eighth foal; closely related to 1m2f-12.4f winner Derevo (inc AW/KSA; RPR 106), half-sister to five winners including Babouche (6f inc 2yo Group 1; 117), Zarinsk (6f-1m inc Group 2; 115) and Society Lion (6f-1m inc 2yo/AW; 102); those three all won first-time out for this yard; dam 7f/1m (Listed) winner (103).

Bought for 30,000euros as a yearling; twelfth foal; closely related to 7f winner Risk Taker, (RPR 85), half-sister to winners Western Australia (7f 2yo/1m5f Listed; 112), Hoarding (7f-1m2f inc 2yo/Listed; 101) and Strada Facendo (7f; 86); dam 7f winner (75).

Fourth foal; sister to 7f AW winner Stellenbosch (RPR 85), half-sister to winners Sugar Island (7f/1m 2yo inc Group 3; RPR 103) and Mother Nature (11.3f; 101); dam 11.3f winner (90), sister to winners Minding (1,000 Guineas/Oaks) and Tuesday (Oaks).

5.45.betting_forecast: 4/1 Bad Boy Rizz, 5/1 Allsortz, 13/2 Treasured Royal, 7/1 Amiata, 8/1 Wearing Stars, 10/1 Coincidental Glory, Joyful Tidings,
5.45.spotlight_verdict: The Hartys won this race for similar connections two years ago and maybe they've had an eye on it for FONTAINE KHALED who will enjoy getting back on nicer ground and has a feather weight to carry. At the other end of the handicap, Bad Boy Rizz and Allsortz are respected along with Treasured Royal who drops down from stakes company. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: Looked exciting when winning AW maiden over 7f but, in retrospect, didn't beat a great deal; bumped into a smart horse next time; well held both starts this year, beaten 9l in Madrid Handicap on latest; drops to 6f and better ground a help, as might be cheekpieces.
horses.breeding: b f Sands Of Mali - Backstreet Girl

horses.spotlight_comment: Fair efforts on turf last term; won 6f AW maiden on second run back and that form was franked last week; mention of July Sales afterwards wouldn't be hugely encouraging, but perhaps it would be wrong to read too much into that.
horses.breeding: b g Bated Breath - Sub Sahara

horses.spotlight_comment: AW maiden winner over 6f in December; beaten just under 5l in Cork 5f rated contest; handicap debut.
Consistent in sprint maidens last year; off the mark over 5f when last seen at Navan in October; ground was soft then, but goes on good ground too; handicap debut.
horses.breeding: ch c Bungle Inthejungle - Clifton Dancer

horses.spotlight_comment: Consistent but exposed compared to most of these; 7f AW nursery winner on final start last term and second in 1m claimer at Gowran on return; has placed form at this trip but probably vulnerable at it.

Nice run in a good-ground Curragh maiden last year; well held both handicap starts lately, but a hint of promise under quiet handling last time and yard won this two years ago; wouldn't be too quick to dismiss her.

Beat smart performer when winning 5f maiden on debut last term and ran well behind recent Greenham winner in sales' contest next time; held in handicaps thus far; fitter for Cork comeback having been gelded last autumn, but Carroll prefers stablemate.
Has twice gone close in 6f handicaps at Dundalk; fourth when favourite there last time; up in grade now, so no easy task; headgear applied for the first time.
horses.breeding: b g Kodi Bear - Mienvee Flyer

horses.spotlight_comment: Maiden was runner-up three times in a row at Dundalk over the winter; not as good in recent AW starts; had ok form on fast turf when trained in Britain last term.
Maiden winner over this sort of trip at Navan; ran okay in AW Listed contest over 5f, not so good over 6f at Newmarket when last seen in late October; sights lowered here on handicap debut.
Twice placed over 6f on AW late last year; should come on from reappearance fourth at Cork (5f, soft); handicap debut.
Won at 20-1 on handicap debut over 6f at Dundalk in October; down the field on last month's return over 7f at same course, in race won by stablemate; coming back to 6f looks the right move.

6.15.betting_forecast: 100/30 Bishopton, 4/1 Staysound Susie, 9/2 Tango Flare, 11/2 Headmaster, 13/2 Indigo Dream, 10/1 Valiant Force, 12/1
6.15.spotlight_verdict: The drop back to 6f is a slight concern for the recent Dundalk winner Bishopton and Staysound Susie, another recent winner, will need a big career-best off her revised mark. Eddie Lynam runs three and it might be worth taking a chance on his C&D winner HEAVENLY POWER who is 4lb below his last win and should be sharper for his comeback run at the Curragh. Indigo Dream and City House are others worth considering. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Won her third handicap off 77 at Chepstow last August (5f, gd-sft); hit with an 11lb hike for an Ayr Listed sixth in September; no impact in Listed races here and at Bath the last twice and on a tough mark returned to handicap company.

Resumed progress on seasonal return when a 0.5l winner at Dundalk last month; record of 1-10 on turf, the win coming in a 7f handicap at Down Royal; drop back to 6f a bit of a worry here; cheekpieces go on.

Smart turf form for George Scott in Bahrain early last year; best run for Ado McGuinness over 6f at Dundalk on penultimate but only beat two rivals home at Newcastle on latest; potentially well handicapped on return to turf and not dismissed.
horses.breeding: b g Night Of Thunder - Impala

horses.spotlight_comment: Bounced back to form from out of the blue to win the Scurry at the Curragh last July; has generally struggled since and well beaten in both starts this season at the Curragh; needs a revival.

One of three for yard; won two for William Haggas, a 7f Haydock maiden (good) and a 7f Newbury handicap (soft) on his final run for that yard in October; bought for 48,000gns later that month and the market can guide on first start for new yard.

One of three for yard; five-time winner, the most recent over C&D (yielding) in October 2024 off 4lb higher; shaped as though in need of the run last time at the Curragh and should be much sharper now; interesting.
horses.breeding: b g Dark Angel - Girl Power

horses.spotlight_comment: 3yo; two wins last year included the Ballyhane Stakes over this C&D (gd-yld); came up short in Listed company subsequently and has been gelded; probably best watched on handicap debut and seasonal return.
horses.breeding: b g Nando Parrado - Madam Macie

horses.spotlight_comment: 0-6 on turf but in fine form on AW; won 7f Dundalk maiden in December and creditable efforts in valuable 7f Newcastle handicaps the last twice; drop to 6f a query but can't be discounted.

One of three for yard; six-time winner, the last three of which have come at the Curragh; testing ground a valid excuse for poor run at that venue on seasonal return but remains 4lb above last win and may need more help from the handicapper.
Five-time winner at 5f-6f on good and soft ground; is 2lb lower than when winning at Bellewstown in October but has struggled badly in both starts this season; others arrive in better form.
Career-best on latest to land a nice pot at the Curragh (6f, sft-hvy) under this rider, her fourth win; ground-versatile but she'll need to improve again to follow up off a career-high mark of 90.
horses.breeding: b m U S Navy Flag - Eucharist

horses.spotlight_comment: Finished last season in excellent form with a 50-1 win in the Bold Lad at the Curragh (6f, yielding) and a 1.75l second in a Listed race here (6f, yielding); off since October and has needed his comeback run in the past two seasons.

Sole win on turf in the 2023 Norfolk Stakes; has won five conditions races at Dundalk since, the most recent a 4.25l win over 5f in February; well beaten at Lingfield and Newcastle the last twice and others arrive in better form.
horses.breeding: ro h Malibu Moon - Vigui's Heart

6.45.betting_forecast: 5/4 Force Noir, 3/1 Mr Montauk, 9/2 Lady Patrona, 8/1 Bit Of A Buzz, 12/1 The Scallionator, 16/1 No Time Faults, 33/1 Whammy.
6.45.spotlight_verdict: Amo Racing always run a smart type in the opening 2yo maiden of the season at the Curragh and, narrowly denied when odds-on there, FORCE NOIR (nap) will be hard to beat with the run behind him. Mr Montauk and Bit Of A Buzz might make him work for it while Lady Patrona is the most likely of contender of the three fillies in the line-up. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: Cost 25,000euros as a yearling; second foal; dam seven-race maiden (placed 1m1f in France), half-sister to winners Azmeel (1m2f Group 3), Baisse (German 1m Listed, dam of smart 7f-1m2f winner Best Of Days) and Apache Storm (6f/7f inc 2yo, dam of 1m2f Group 3 winner Galen).

A March foal and cost 130,000euros as a yearling; beaten a head at the Curragh on opening day of the season, rallying late on; Amo Racing had won that race with smart types in the previous three seasons, and should be hard to beat here.

Made 11,000gns as a yearling; fifth foal; half-sister to winners Loch Tay (7.5f 2yo/HK 1m dirt; RPR 91), Circo Massimo (French/Belgian 1m1f-11.5f inc AW; 81), Aquiliae (French 1m4f) and Palace Party (German 7.7f); dam unraced sister to 1m 2yo Group 1 winner Proportional

Seventh foal; brother to winners Sergeant Wilko (5f/6f inc 2yo/AW; RPR 101) and Jungle Monarch (Qatari 6f), half-brother to three winners inc Coul Queen (7f inc 2yo; 95) and Stately Home (1m inc AW; 88); dam well held 7f-9.4f (49); yard's first 2yo runner won lately.

Made 20,000gns as a yearling; fourth foal; dam 6f 2yo winner (inc Listed; RPR 97), half-sister to useful 7f/1m winner Caelis, out of maiden half-sister to 1m2f Group 2 winner Fracas and useful 7f/1m winner Tregaron.

Was 10,000euros yearling; fifth foal; half-brother to 6f 2yo/7f winner McTenett (RPR 91); dam 7f winner (81), half-sister to Listed winners Shamshon (5f 2yo) and Boerhan (1m), out of 7f/1m winning half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Millisle.
Kodi Bear filly showed early pace before weakening when well-beaten fourth of 5 in AW maiden.

7.15.betting_forecast: 7/2 Mission Central, 4/1 Bucanero Fuerte, 11/2 King Cuan, 13/2 Fahrenheit Seven, 9/1 Getreadytorumble, 10/1 Big Gossey, 12/1
7.15.spotlight_verdict: A competitive heat. The British raiders Fahrenheit Seven and Getreadytorumble are very much respected but the top-rated BUCANERO FUERTE should be much sharper for his comeback run at Cork and is taken to get back to winning ways. It is interesting that Billy Lee prefers Bonus Time over her higher-rated stablemate King Cuan and the recent Curragh handicap winner Bodhi Bear is another one that could go well, as could the 3yo filly Cardiff By The Sea. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Marvelous veteran showed he retained all his ability when winning for the eleventh time in the Listed Gladness Stakes at the Curragh (7f, sft-hvy) a month ago; however, has come up short in the last three renewals of this race and 5f probably sharp enough for him these days.

Gelded in the off-season and won on seasonal return for the second year running when landing a Curragh handicap (5f, sft-hvy); this is harder and has lots to find on the figures, but he's relatively lightly raced and there could be more to come.

One of two for yard; two 6f wins last year, making all to score in a Curragh maiden (good) and a conditions race here (gd-yld); disappointed upped to 7f when last seen at York and loads to find on the figures on her first try at 5f, but interesting that Billy Lee seemingly prefers her to King Cuan.
horses.breeding: b f Too Darn Hot - Karijini

horses.spotlight_comment: Top class 2yo returned from aborted stud career last year and won a C&D Listed race (good) and a Curragh Group 3 (6f, good); fine third in the Group 1 Flying Five before a below-par run at the Breeders' Cup; soft ground not ideal for seasonal reappearance and better expected now; chance.
horses.breeding: b h Wootton Bassett - Frida La Blonde

horses.spotlight_comment: 3yo filly whose best effort in three runs as a 2yo came when a 1.75l fourth of 23 in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot; last of seven in a C&D Listed race in July and not seen again until landing a 5f maiden at Cork (soft) 23 days ago; gets all the allowances and that maiden form was boosted at Navan on Saturday.
horses.breeding: b f St Mark's Basilica - Piece Of Paradise

horses.spotlight_comment: Capable of smart form on his day but hasn't won since August 2022 and was well held behind Bodhi Bear on his seasonal reappearance; hopes pinned on cheekpieces sparking a revival.

British raider arrives in terrific form having won back-to-back 5f AW handicaps at Newcastle off 92 and Southwell off 99; effective on good ground; probably needs to improve again on first run in Listed company, but can't be discounted.

Five-time winner at 5f-6f on good and yielding ground; well beaten on seasonal return at the Curragh (6f, soft) but may have needed that; likely to be ridden to try and nick some black type and could outrun her likely odds if they go a strong gallop.

British raider from a yard that has started the season strongly; highly progressive last year, winning a maiden and two handicaps before a close third in the Listed Rous Stakes at Ascot (5f, soft); ground-versatile and, while he has a bit to find on paper, can't be dismissed.
horses.breeding: gr g Rumble Inthejungle - El Che

horses.spotlight_comment: Classy sprinter for Clive Cox and won a Listed and a Group 2 for that yard; decent run on debut for this stable at Dundalk in February, but behind a few of these when tailed off at Cork last time; needs to leave that well behind.

One of two for yard; has won four times at 6f-7f and is 2-2 at this track; sole win last year came in a three-runner auction race at Fairyhouse (6f, good); subsequently placed in Listed and Group 3 company; had a few of these behind when a 3.5l third at Cork (6f, soft) on seasonal return; sharper now but has never won over 5f and Billy Lee prefers Bonus Time.

1-12 on turf but has had a few near misses, including when beaten a short head in a 5f Curragh handicap (soft) last time; ran well over C&D (yielding) last October, but rated 84 and looks to be up against it in this company.
horses.breeding: b f Inns Of Court - Trisara

horses.spotlight_comment: 3yo won three of six starts as a juvenile, including a Group 3 at the Curragh (6f, gd-yld) and a valuable conditions race at Ascot (6f, good); struggled when dropped to 5f at the Breeders' Cup, extending his record to 0-3 at the minimum trip; entitled to be thereabouts on ratings, but others make more appeal.
horses.breeding: b g No Nay Never - Thar She Blows

horses.spotlight_comment: Former Flying Five winner landed this race in 2023 and 2024; lost form in the second half of 2024 and missed all of last season; entitled to need this run after such a long layoff.

Five-time winner best with a bit of cut in the ground; sole win last season came in a Listed heat at this venue (6f, yielding); may have needed his comeback at Cork and likes it here, but would probably like to see some rain.

Has won three handicaps at 6f, including one here; not disgraced when fourth in a 6f Cork Listed race on latest, 2.25l behind King Cuan; needs to find a bit more dropped back in trip in the first-time blinkers.

7.45.betting_forecast: 11/4 Trojan Warrior, 9/2 Felix Guido, 13/2 Alphecca, 15/2 Bobby McGee, 8/1 How'Sthebai, 17/2 Invincible Will, 10/1 Controlled,
7.45.spotlight_verdict: Held in good regard by his stable, HOW'STHEBAI should do well in handicaps this term and is interesting off bottom weight. Trojan Warrior has to give 19lb to the selection but is greatly feared in first-time headgear, while Alphecca's connections are bidding for their third win in four years in this particular contest. Polish recruit Felix Guido is impossible to assess but is, reportedly, well thought of by his trainer. [Mark Nunan]

horses.spotlight_comment: Progressive on easy ground in the autumn; off the mark over this trip in early October and won valuable restricted contest over 7f here just six days later; yard, and owner, have won two of the last three renewals.
Ran nice races in early summer at two; back from lengthy layoff, and having been gelded, to win Gowran maiden (7f, soft); first go at a mile.
Ex-Ballydoyle performer won 5f maiden at this track last term and fine second in Madrid Handicap over 7f here on his return; well beaten last time and vulnerable off this mark; best form on soft.
horses.breeding: b g No Nay Never - Ultrasonic

horses.spotlight_comment: Unbeaten in three starts in Poland at up to 6.5f, making all each time; impossible to assess but respect for the trainer means he can't be taken lightly; market useful.
Off the mark in 1m AW maiden in October on last of three juvenile outings; seasonal and handicap debut; 1lb wrong.
horses.breeding: ch g Bated Breath - Irish Madam

horses.spotlight_comment: Solid nursery performer on easy ground, winning over 7f at the Curragh; good effort on return when second at Cork (1m, soft to heavy).
horses.breeding: b g Invincible Army - Lady Nancy

horses.spotlight_comment: Clear of the rest when chasing home Bobby McGee at Gowran (7f, soft); handed mark of 81 for handicap debut.
Shaped well over 6f on debut and then won AW maiden over 1m in November; looks yard's second-string on jockey arrangements; seasonal and handicap debut.
AW maiden winner over 1m in early March; later that month was beaten around 5l in Madrid Handicap here over 7f; better ground this time will help.
horses.breeding: b g Nando Parrado - Pretty Face

horses.spotlight_comment: Beat a smart rival in 6f Curragh maiden (heavy) in October; only 6-1 for 7f Guineas trial at Leopardstown, still looked green and didn't land a blow; could be a different proposition in a handicap with that run behind him and headgear added.

8.15.betting_forecast: 9/4 Glyfada, 3/1 Cape Primrose, 100/30 Arrietty, 6/1 Sounds Great, 12/1 Charm Of Venice, Shambata, 20/1 Soigne, 22/1 French
8.15.spotlight_verdict: A few of these have claims. Cape Primrose and Arrietty should be thereabouts and Sounds Great is also worth considering but GLYFADA shaped very nicely on debut at the Curragh and, with improvement likely to be forthcoming, she gets the vote. The nicely-bred Gavin Cromwell newcomers French Blond and Soigne need checking in the market. [Dave Stephens]

horses.spotlight_comment: Rated 77; runner-up in three of four starts on AW including at this trip the last twice at Dundalk earlier this year; well held by Cape Primrose on sole turf start at Thurles on debut but that rival had the benefit of a previous run; in the mix if ready after break.
horses.breeding: b f Lope De Vega - Sommorell

horses.spotlight_comment: Well-bred filly is rated 79 after three starts; just under 6l ahead of Arrietty when runner-up at Thurles on second start last year; soft ground may not have suited when disappointing on return at Gowran; should go well in first-time cheekpieces.
horses.breeding: b f St Mark's Basilica - Again

horses.spotlight_comment: Showed nothing on debut at Leopardstown in October (7f, yielding); better effort at Dundalk (1m) in January when a 3.25l fifth of 14; moves up in trip with Keane a notable booking, but more needed.
33-1 for her debut at Dundalk (1m) in November and not disgraced; moves up in distance for her turf debut and is probably best watched unless the market speaks.
Sent off at 200-1 when finishing in mid-field on debut at Leopardstown 12 days ago (1m, yld-sft); should improve for that initial experience but lots more needed up in trip.

Almanzor filly; E62,000 yearling; dam 5.7f-1m winner (inc 2yo Group 3; RPR 106), half-sister to winners Keeper's Heart (Listed-placed 1m 2yo), Elite Legion (7f 2yo) and Muntahez (1m1f), out of Listed-placed 6f 2yo winner; nicely-bred newcomer worth a market check.

Beaten 0.5l on debut by a more experienced rival at the Curragh (1m1f) on very testing ground when a 4-1 shot; pedigree suggests this ground and step up in trip will suit and she is a leading contender.

New Bay filly; dam 7f winner (RPR 87), half-sister to winners Shembala (French 1m6f Listed) and Sheberghan (10.5f), out of Group-placed 7f winner; debutante from in form yard needs checking in the market.

Ghaiyyath filly; E52,000 yearling; half-sister to winners Conviction (7f AW 2yo; RPR 76), Angelica K (1m AW; 65) and Lord Howe (Italian 1m/8.7f inc AW); dam 8.5f AW winner, sister to 1m Group 1 winner Timepiece, half-sister to 1m2f 2yo Group 1 winner Passage Of Time; preferred by Gary Carroll; check the market.
Identical RPRs (75) when fourth on debut at Galway (9.5f, sft-hvy) last October and when a 1.5l second of 7 on seasonal return at Gowran (9.5f, soft); place claims if acting on this sounder surface.
